mig.intro: For when a server expires or you change machines: make a migration code on the old server and paste it on this page on the new one. Only data moves (sites, apps, databases, VMs), never the machine's own setup (partitions, mounts, network cards); the new machine's disks are checked first, and you are told before anything is written if it does not fit.
mig.left_behind: Not moved: partitions and mounts, RAID, swap, network cards and IPs, hostname, SSH settings (they belong to the machine); Cloudflare Tunnels and Wharf publishing are set up again on the new machine; monitoring history and the audit log stay on the old panel. Database tuning is worked out again for the new machine's memory.

wharf.our_fp: Berth's fingerprint (Wharf's pairing page shows it for you to compare):
wharf.pair_failed: Pairing did not finish: {reason}. Start again with Approve on Wharf.
wharf.pair_how: Once paired: router port mappings follow your sites, bans sync both ways, alerts come from one place, you jump between panels without signing in, and you see the router's view here. Enter Wharf's address, confirm its certificate, then approve on Wharf.
wharf.pair_title: Pair with a Wharf router panel
wharf.pick_fp: Wharf presented these certificates. Compare with the fingerprint Wharf shows under Settings → Security, then pick the one to pin (the CA is best):
wharf.public_cert: A public certificate from {issuer}, valid for this name: checked by name from now on, renewals keep working. Wharf's own certificate is accepted too when reached directly on the LAN.
wharf.public_fp_note: No fingerprint to compare: the one on Wharf's pairing page belongs to its own local certificate, used on its LAN address (e.g. https://wharf.lan:7080). Its public name presents the public certificate above, so they differ by design.
wharf.publish_hint: Mappings point at this host's router address {ip}. Port mapping: WAN port → this host's 443. 443 splitting: when Wharf's proxy owns 443, it passes these names through (Berth keeps the certificates). Removed when the site is deleted.
wharf.super_only: Only a super administrator can pair with Wharf
wharf.unpair_how: After unpairing {name}, both tokens stop working at once.
wharf.unpair_keep: Keep the mappings Berth made (as ordinary Wharf mappings); otherwise delete them
wharf.user_map: User mapping (for sign-in links from Wharf)
wharf.user_map_hint: Wharf users without a mapping cannot jump in. After the jump, the mapped Berth user's permissions apply.
wharfp.f_build_d: Optional proxy extension, DDNS, port forwards limited by country — no extra Linux box needed.
wharfp.f_control_d: Give a friend a port range or a device without the root password; every step is audited and can be undone.
wharfp.f_diagnose_d: Route maps, packet capture with diagnosis, monitors and alerts, LAN scans — evidence you can hand to your ISP.
wharfp.f_see_d: Every device has a name and type; see whether it is streaming, using AI or gaming, and which countries its traffic goes to.
wharfp.key_auth_hint: Both sides sign with a key id; the token never travels, so a proxy such as Cloudflare never sees it
wharfp.lead: A LuCI app on the router using only OpenWrt's own mechanisms — it never restarts the network. Every device has a name and you see what it talks to; hand a port range to a friend without the root password; route tracing, packet capture diagnosis and monitors built in. Free and open source, like Berth.
wharfp.pair_title: Pair Wharf and Berth in three steps
wharfp.s1_d: Download the ipk for your router's architecture from the latest release, upload it to /tmp and run:
wharfp.s1_req: Needs OpenWrt 22.03+, 512 MB of memory, x86_64 / aarch64 / arm. LuCI → Services → Wharf then shows its address (https://router-ip:7080 by default).
wharfp.s2_d: On Wharf's Berth page click "Let Berth ask to pair (10 minutes)", then click Ask to pair below: both show the same check code; Allow on Wharf and it is done. Not on the same LAN? Use "Or pair by address".
wharfp.s3_d: Check both show the same code and click Allow on Wharf; pairing finishes here by itself (pairing by address: agree on Wharf's page and you come back). You are then told the panel's new address and taken to add a Passkey there.
wharfp.shot_alt: Wharf overview: live speed, devices online, where today's traffic went
wharfp.t_alerts_d: Pick one side to notify you; alerts from both go out once.
wharfp.t_bans_d: IPs Berth bans for scanning or brute force are blocked at the router too, and the other way round.
wharfp.t_ddns_d: The router knows first when the address changes; let Wharf keep your DDNS names.
wharfp.t_forward_d: New sites get a router port forward or 443 split automatically; removed with the site.
wharfp.t_sso_d: Open Wharf from Berth already signed in; users are matched by name.
wharfp.t_traffic_d: See this server's traffic and scans as the router sees them.
wharfp.tagline: An OpenWrt router panel for the whole family and several admins: clear to read, safe to share, easy to troubleshoot.
